purpose: Identify the most important things CFA-01 failed to characterize during bootstrap and the minimum context/tooling needed to operate those gaps without overengineering.

methodology.priorityScale: P0/P1/P2 where P0 = foundational semantic gap; P1 = major operating gap; P2 = important future gap.
methodology.epistemicStatus: DERIVED from repository evidence plus bootstrap conversation; not canonical architecture.

topGaps.name: Temporal World semantics
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We repeatedly mentioned events, states, revisions, replay and time, but never characterized the semantic model of time itself.
topGaps.whyItMatters: Without a temporal model, World state, relationship validity, freshness, context, Work deadlines, external observation, history and 'what was true at T' can collapse into timestamps or storage revisions.
questions: What is valid-time versus observation/system-time?
Is an Event a World object, an observation, a causal record, or several distinct roles?
How is State derived from events/revisions?
How are temporal relationship assertions represented?
What does 'current' mean when sources disagree or arrive late?
neededContext: Agentic temporal substrate and wake semantics
neededTooling: Semantic Lens temporal mode: inspect-at(T), timeline, before/after, valid-from/to and observation-time comparison.
Deterministic temporal fixture set for World reconstruction at multiple times.
topGaps.firstProof: Take one Project/Task relationship through creation, change, archive and later external observation; reconstruct the World at T1/T2/T3.

topGaps.name: Observation → World reconciliation
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We identified external source identity and correspondence, but did not yet define the semantic ladder from observation to assertion to canonical World state.
topGaps.whyItMatters: Productivity tools and providers continuously expose partial, delayed, conflicting or lossy observations. A coherent World requires explicit reconciliation rather than parser output becoming truth.
questions: What exactly is an observation?
When can an observation support an assertion?
When does an assertion become canonical World state?
How are conflicting observations retained?
How are merge/split/collision decisions represented?
What does write-back confirmation mean versus external write success?
neededContext: CFA-02 data continuity and reconciliation material
CFA-06 provider/source identity and realization evidence
neededTooling: Semantic Lens reconcile mode: source observation → correspondence candidate → assertion → canonical object/relationship → evidence.
Correspondence test harness with positive, ambiguous, conflicting and lossy fixtures.
topGaps.firstProof: Use a productivity object present in two providers with different names, one stale observation and one contradictory relationship.

topGaps.name: Negative space / absence semantics
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We treated unknown as valid, but did not distinguish the kinds of 'not present' that are essential to World reasoning.
topGaps.whyItMatters: Not found, not observed, inaccessible, deleted, archived, never existed and known absent are semantically different. Context and automation cannot safely reason about absence without these distinctions.
questions: Does not-found mean unknown, absent, or query failure?
How is inaccessible distinguished from nonexistent?
What is the semantic meaning of deletion versus disappearance from a provider?
Can absence itself be evidence?
When may a context omit an object because it is confidently absent?
neededTooling: Semantic Lens explain-absence mode returning one explicit state: UNKNOWN | NOT_OBSERVED | INACCESSIBLE | ABSENT | DELETED | ARCHIVED | FILTERED | ERROR.
Negative-space fixtures and falsifiers.
topGaps.firstProof: Query for an object that is deleted locally, missing from a provider, inaccessible by scope, and simply not observed.

topGaps.name: Productivity-domain semantics
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We mapped productivity providers into generic Objects but did not sufficiently characterize the semantics of the things people actually organize around: task, commitment, goal, project, event, document, conversation, person and resource.
topGaps.whyItMatters: A universal object envelope is insufficient if VIVIM cannot tell a Task from Work, an Event from an observation, or a Commitment from a message mentioning one.
questions: What makes something a Task versus Work?
Is Commitment a first-class World concept or a relationship/role?
What distinguishes Goal, Project and Space?
Is Calendar Event a World event or a domain object with event semantics?
When does a Message create or support a Task/Commitment relationship?
neededContext: World Object taxonomy and relationship model
Destination journeys around projects and continuity
neededTooling: Semantic Lens type/relationship comparison for productivity concepts.
Small domain fixture corpus spanning email, task, calendar, document, project and repository.
topGaps.firstProof: Model one real end-to-end productivity chain: message → commitment → task → Work → result → evidence → project state.

topGaps.name: Attention as a World/context participant
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We noted Attention in the bootstrap prompt but did not actually characterize its relation to World, current Context, Work and standing Intent.
topGaps.whyItMatters: A persistent assistant cannot simply retrieve relevant objects. It needs a semantic notion of salience without turning attention into hidden task state or UI-only focus.
questions: Is Attention a World concept, a projection, or a policy-governed derived state?
What creates salience: user intent, focus, world change, Work state, time?
Does attention have identity/history?
How does attention become Context without becoming authority?
What is the difference between Focus and Attention?
neededTooling: Semantic Lens salience mode showing why an item is relevant to current context.
Temporal attention fixtures for changing salience over time.
topGaps.firstProof: Given the same World at three times, explain why different items are salient without changing canonical object meaning.

topGaps.name: World Query / Address contract
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We named semantic addressing and traversal repeatedly, but did not actually characterize the destination query/address language enough to make the Semantic Lens implementable.
topGaps.whyItMatters: This is the bridge from semantic understanding to actual operation. Without it, each caller will invent its own selectors and traversal grammar.
questions: What is the smallest universal query target?
How are identity, predicate, time and scope expressed?
How are traversal depth and cardinality bounded?
How are ambiguous matches represented?
Can every query explain its basis and result scope?
neededTooling: Semantic Lens query parser/AST with deterministic execution over a fixed snapshot.
Query explain output: resolved identities, predicates traversed, scope, bounds and rejected candidates.
topGaps.firstProof: Resolve one natural-language target into a deterministic structured traversal and show why alternative candidates were rejected.

topGaps.name: Semantic change / migration semantics
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We covered identity continuity and evolution, but did not characterize the difference between changing a shape, changing meaning, replacing an object, and reinterpreting a relationship.
topGaps.whyItMatters: Without this distinction, evolution tooling will either over-migrate or silently change World meaning.
questions: What is semantic versioning versus schema versioning?
When does a changed predicate preserve relation identity?
How is reinterpretation different from replacement?
What must happen to existing Context recipes and graph projections?
What is reversible and what requires explicit owner decision?
neededTooling: Semantic Lens impact mode extended with semantic-change classification.
Small mutation/reinterpretation/replace/retire fixture suite.
topGaps.firstProof: Apply four different changes to one concept and verify that the tool produces different impact/reconciliation requirements.

topGaps.name: Scope / visibility / multi-principal World semantics
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We treated authority as a neighbor, but did not sufficiently define how visibility and ownership scope alter the World projection itself, especially for future shared environments.
topGaps.whyItMatters: The destination includes future multi-sovereign/shared experiences. World membership cannot be assumed global when access, ownership or delegation changes what is visible.
questions: Is visibility a World property, an authority projection, or both?
How does a World differ across principals while referring to the same external thing?
Can two projections expose different relationship sets without contradicting each other?
How should Context explain filtered visibility?
neededContext: Product Instance and future multi-sovereign material
neededTooling: Semantic Lens scoped-view mode: same subject/query under explicit principal/scope snapshots.
Cross-scope consistency tests.
topGaps.firstProof: Compare the same Project under owner, delegated agent and limited collaborator scopes.

topGaps.name: Semantic Lens source-snapshot discipline
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We designed the Lens conceptually but did not define how one inspection proves exactly which repository/evidence snapshot it read.
topGaps.whyItMatters: Without source snapshot identity, deterministic claims about a Lens result can become unrepeatable as documents and indexes change.
neededTooling: Snapshot manifest automatically attached to every Lens result: repository SHA, source file SHAs, index versions and query/options.
Replay command that regenerates the same result from the captured snapshot where possible.
topGaps.firstProof: Run the same Lens query twice against a pinned snapshot and verify equivalent output and source basis.

topGaps.name: Context quality without hidden ranking authority
topGaps.whatWeMissed: We described bounded Context but did not test how relevance/ranking can be useful without becoming a hidden semantic or authority system.
topGaps.whyItMatters: Context assembly will eventually need ordering, budgets and optimization. Those mechanisms can silently mutate meaning if not constrained.
questions: What is semantic inclusion versus optimization ranking?
Can ranking reorder evidence without changing epistemic meaning?
How are excluded candidates explained?
What happens when budget forces omission of a high-confidence item?
neededTooling: Semantic Lens context-dry-run mode that shows included/excluded candidates and the reason each was selected or omitted.
Budget perturbation test suite.
topGaps.firstProof: Generate the same Context under multiple budgets and show that semantic truth and provenance remain invariant while only selection changes.

semanticLensEvolution.principle: Extend one Lens rather than create ten specialized tools.
implementationSequence: V0 repository snapshot + source adapters + inspect/trace/explain

bootstrapCloseout.whatWasMissing: CFA-01 had strong structural orientation but insufficiently characterized temporal, observational, negative-space, productivity, attention, query, and semantic-change semantics.
bootstrapCloseout.mostImportantNewInsight: A World is not merely objects plus edges. It is objects and relationships interpreted across time, observation provenance, scope, and change, with explicit uncertainty and reconstructability.
bootstrapCloseout.smallestUsefulNextStep: Do not build a full ontology or graph runtime. First build/prove the repository-backed Semantic Lens against the four highest-risk gaps: temporal, observation/reconciliation, negative-space and query/address.
bootstrapCloseout.finalBootstrapStatus: SEED READY FOR PAUSE; SUBSTANTIVE ARCHITECTURAL IDENTITY REMAINS PROVISIONAL UNTIL OWNER ALIGNMENT.
